title: RequirementRefinementResult
description: Canonical structured output contract for the Requirements Refinement capability (ba-qa-agent + the requirement-analysis skill). One instance of this schema is the complete, self-contained result of refining exactly one requirement identity (a Jira issue, an already-supplied Jira story, or free-text/BRD content). This schema defines the CONTRACT only — no persistence mechanism is implied or wired up here; scripts/save_agent_output.py's Markdown-artifact mechanism is unaffected until a separate task wires this JSON contract into it. Every object that can assert a fact carries its provenance via evidence_ids referencing the top-level `evidence` registry; nothing may claim 'confirmed' status without a resolvable, appropriately-typed evidence reference (see the confirmed-requires-evidence rule enforced by scripts/validate_requirement_refinement_result.py, which performs the cross-reference and business-rule checks this schema's static shape cannot express on its own).

run_id.description: Matches the run-id format already minted by scripts/save_agent_output.py (RUN_ID_RE), so this contract's identifiers stay compatible with the platform's existing persistence convention even though this schema does not persist anything itself.

requirement_id.description: Stable identifier for the requirement being refined: the Jira issue key when one exists, otherwise a caller-supplied or deterministically-derived identifier for the free-text/BRD input. Never fabricated when none was supplied — use a locally-unique placeholder and record the absence as an Unknown, do not invent a Jira-key-shaped string.

EvidenceSourceType.description: Where a piece of evidence actually came from. Must match one of the input/retrieval shapes the requirement-analysis skill and ba-qa-agent actually support — never a source type implying a capability (e.g. Confluence, a CI system) that isn't wired up.

KnowledgeFabricTier.description: Policy applicability tier, required on every evidence item whose source_type is knowledge_fabric; null/absent otherwise.

RetrievalTool.description: The exact tool that produced this evidence, or 'user_supplied' for content pasted/handed directly rather than retrieved. Restricted to tools actually granted to ba-qa-agent today — never a Jira write tool, a Confluence tool, or an unregistered Knowledge Fabric tool (detect_conflicts, detect_gaps, trace_requirement, etc. do not exist and must never appear here).

ClaimBasis.description: Provenance category for a single statement. 'confirmed' is only earned by a resolvable evidence_ids reference to an appropriately-typed, actually-retrieved evidence item (see the validator) — it can never be assigned to fill a silence.

EvidenceRefList.description: References into the top-level `evidence[].id` registry. Every id here must resolve to a real evidence entry — a dangling reference is a claim of evidence that was never retrieved, which this contract forbids.

locator.description: document_id (Knowledge Fabric), Jira field name or issue key, repo-relative file path, or a description of the supplied text's origin.

tier.description: Required (non-null) when source_type is knowledge_fabric; must be null for every other source_type.

excerpt.description: The actual quoted or closely-paraphrased text that was retrieved — never left blank. A citation with no excerpt is not grounding, it's a label.

retrieved_at_run.description: run_id in which this evidence was actually captured, when reused from a prior run's artifact (e.g. version-comparison evidence); null when captured in this run.

related_evidence_ids.description: Optional, informative-only evidence that motivated an assumption/recommendation without confirming it. Never counted as confirmation.

rationale.description: Required when basis is not 'confirmed' — why this was inferred, recommended, or left unknown.

Claim.description: A single provenanced statement. evidence_ids may only be non-empty when basis == 'confirmed' — a non-confirmed claim cannot carry confirming evidence, structurally preventing an assumption from being dressed up as a confirmed fact.

BusinessRule.description: Extends Claim. A business rule may only be basis == 'confirmed' when it is quoted/paraphrased from the requirement text, supplied AC, or a Directly-applicable Knowledge Fabric document (enforced by the validator, not just this shape) — this is the concrete mechanism that satisfies 'never let an unsupported business rule look confirmed'.

blocking_clarification_question_ids.description: References into clarification_questions[].id. Required non-empty when status == 'blocked_by_clarification'; must be empty otherwise.

AcceptanceCriterion.description: Every acceptance criterion is exactly one of confirmed / proposed / blocked_by_clarification — never merged, never a fourth silent state. 'confirmed' requires resolvable, appropriately-typed evidence (validator-checked); 'blocked_by_clarification' requires at least one real clarification question blocking it, not just an assertion that it's blocked.

requirement_ref.description: Jira key, artifact path, or other concrete pointer to the related requirement — never a vague description standing in for an actual reference.

search_scope_limitation.description: Mandatory statement of what search scope this duplicate check did NOT cover (e.g. no project-wide JQL search was run) — a duplicate-candidate entry may never imply an exhaustive search occurred.

Conflict.description: The four-part conflict record. Deliberately has no 'resolution', 'winner', or 'resolved_by' field anywhere in this shape (additionalProperties: false enforces this) — a conflict cannot be represented as resolved by this contract; only a human, outside this artifact, resolves it.

secondary_type.description: At most one secondary type, and it must differ from primary_type — checked by the validator, since standard JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling fields for inequality.

evidence_of_absence.description: What was searched and came back empty (e.g. a search_knowledge query), supporting the claim that this is genuinely a gap and not an unsearched area.

clarification_question_id.description: Reference into clarification_questions[].id when this gap produced one.

question.description: Must be answerable in one sentence or one decision — never a vague 'please clarify requirements.'

raised_by_id.description: id of the ambiguity note or gaps[] entry that produced this question.

scope_note.description: Must state that this is a high-level candidate only, not a full automation plan — the full layer decision and delegation belongs to automation-agent, never to this contract.

caveat.description: Any 'supplied/unverified' or similar caveat the existing test file itself discloses, carried forward verbatim.

evidence_id.description: Must reference a repo_file evidence entry.

reason_if_not_applicable.description: Required non-null when applicable == false (e.g. 'no existing test evidence found').

search_scope_limitation.description: Mandatory even when applicable == true: this repo grants no project-wide Jira search beyond searchJiraIssuesUsingJql (JQL) plus search_knowledge/repo-local artifacts — state plainly that this is not an exhaustive cross-project search.

downstream_ref.description: An existing_test_mapping entry id or a dependency id, when the chain extends that far. Null otherwise — never a fabricated test/automation reference.

status.description: Always 'candidate' — this contract has no mechanism to mark a traceability chain final. Finalization happens outside this artifact (a downstream Test Authoring/automation stage), never here.

CriticStatus.description: Overall Requirements Critic pass outcome. When more than one would apply, report the most severe in this order: unresolved_issues_remain > escalation_required > revised > clean.

CriticCheckNumber.description: Which of the requirement-analysis skill's fourteen Requirements Critic checks this finding came from (1=original intent preserved ... 14=tool operation claimed but not actually performed).

CriticDisposition.description: 'revise': fixed in place using only evidence already retrieved/supplied in this run — never by upgrading a claim's evidentiary status. 'escalate': requires a human/business decision; recorded as (or linked to) a Conflict/Gap/Clarification Question, never resolved by the agent. 'unresolved': could not be fixed or cleanly reduced to one escalatable decision.

description.description: What the critic found, e.g. 'AC-003 cited kb-004 but kb-004 was never opened via get_context.'

section_ref.description: Which field/id of this same document the finding refers to.

CriticCorrection.description: One entry per 'revise'-disposition finding that was actually fixed. A revise-disposition finding with no matching correction is a contract violation (see validator) — its disposition should have been 'unresolved' instead.

CriticUnresolvedItem.description: One entry per finding with disposition 'escalate' or 'unresolved'.

findings.description: Every problem the Requirements Critic pass actually found, across all fourteen checks — empty only when critic_status is 'clean'.

corrections.description: Never invented to close a finding — a correction may only remove, downgrade, relabel, or reformat, never assert evidence that wasn't actually retrieved.

escalation_required.description: true if and only if at least one finding has disposition 'escalate' — cross-checked by the validator, not just self-reported.

passed.description: Whether scripts/validate_requirement_refinement_result.py ran clean against this document at production time.

violations.description: Verbatim violation messages from the validator, when passed == false. A document may still be delivered with known, disclosed violations (e.g. an unresolved dangling reference explained elsewhere) but must never claim passed == true while violations exist. Distinct from the Requirements Critic pass itself: this is the mechanical, schema-shape check; the critic pass above is the reasoning/quality check.

source_section.description: Which field of this document this confirmed fact was drawn from, e.g. 'business_rules[BR-002]'.

ConfirmedFact.description: Flattened index of every confirmed statement in this document, for fast BA/PO review. Every entry must carry at least one evidence reference by construction.

Assumption.description: No 'evidence_ids' field exists here (only the non-confirming 'related_evidence_ids') — an assumption cannot carry confirming evidence by shape, not just by convention.

why_unresolved.description: Why this could not even be phrased as a useful clarification question.

factors.description: Must match the actual counts elsewhere in this document — cross-checked by the validator. `level` is then bounded by these counts (e.g. any open conflict caps level at 'low'), also validator-enforced, so confidence cannot be asserted independently of the evidence density it claims to summarize.

ReviewStatusValue.description: Deliberately contains no 'approved' value anywhere in this enum. Approval is a human act that happens outside this artifact; this contract has no field capable of representing it.

note.description: Must always be, or clearly imply, 'NOT APPROVED — awaiting BA/PO review', regardless of which status value is set.

text.description: Verbatim reproduction of the requirement as given — never edited or paraphrased here.

jira_fields.description: Raw retrieved/supplied Jira field map, only when source.input_shape is a Jira shape; null for free text/BRD.

evidence_id.description: References the evidence[] entry that is this exact text's source.

added_labels.description: Documents every word/phrase added during normalization that wasn't a direct quote, each with its own basis label.

applicable.description: true only for a Jira input shape; the Original/Refined split does not apply to free-text/BRD input.
